          end

            end

          end

          if enabled
            Rails.application.executor.wrap(**args, &block)

          end
        end

**The Rails Logging Conundrum: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I've been staring at these files (`railtie.rb`, `application.rb`, `development.rb`, and `production.rb`) and the problem statement, and here's what I'm thinking. The core issue is this: how do we get `bin/rails runner` to show the output of a script on the terminal in development without losing the log entries to `log/development.log`? The key is that `config.log_level` is `"debug"` in development. Therefore, we want to capture the script output at the standard output when debugging is enabled.

First, I looked at where `runner do ... end` blocks are executed. I see they are registered with `Writebook::Application`, and executed by `Rails::Command::RunnerCommand` via `load_runner`. This is where we need to insert code! It seems that the *easiest* place to insert it is inside the existing block within `config/application.rb` *inside* the class. This way we ensure the logging action is tied specifically to `bin/rails runner` and not other tasks like `bin/rails server` or `bin/rails console`.

The `BroadcastLogger` is crucial. The idea is to make sure that the `Rails.logger` in `development` *also* outputs to `STDOUT` (and `$stdout`, which is the correct one!). I need to be careful to avoid double-logging, though. So, here's the logic: Only broadcast to `STDOUT` if the `Rails.logger` is *not* already configured to write to `STDOUT` using `ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?`. The trick is that we will be looking at `$stdout`, because the runner command might have swapped the value, if `capture_io` is used in a test.

So, the plan is to add a conditional inside the `runner do ... end` block in `config/application.rb` that checks whether the current logger already outputs to `STDERR` or `STDOUT` and broadcasts if it does not, to a new STDOUT logger with the same formatter and level:

runner do
  unless ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(Rails.logger, STDERR, STDOUT, $stdout)
    console = ActiveSupport::Logger.new($stdout)
    console.formatter = Rails.logger.formatter
    console.level = Rails.logger.level

    if Rails.logger.is_a?(ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger)
      Rails.logger.broadcast_to(console)
    else
      Rails.logger = ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger.new(Rails.logger, console)
    end

The crucial aspect is that setting `console.formatter = Rails.logger.formatter` copies the *same* formatter instance, which is the `TaggedLogging::Formatter`, which ensures tags are preserved across both loggers. I checked the various scenarios and it all works as expected. The log level is also propagated because of the logic in `BroadcastLogger`. The `$stdout` is used instead of `STDOUT` to account for test environments where `$stdout` might be re-assigned. The code takes care of the edge cases. Crucially, the tests are *unaffected* because `load_runner` is not called. We set `console.level = Rails.logger.level` and any change to `Rails.logger.level` will dispatch to the new console logger.

I considered placing this in `config/environments/development.rb` but this has some negative implications. Doing it this way ensures that the solution only affects `bin/rails runner`, avoiding unwanted side-effects on `bin/rails console` and other commands, and it will also work on any environment.

Finally, the `config.log_level` is set to debug in `development` and `Rails.logger.level` is updated. That is the final touch! And finally, I did a rubocop check, and it's happy!

  FTYP_AVIF = "\x00\x00\x00\x1cftypavif\x00\x00\x00\x00avifmif1miaf".b

  PSD = "8BPS" + [ 1 ].pack("n") + "\x00" * 26
  ICO = "\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00" + "\x00" * 16
  SVG = %q(<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="8" height="8"/>)

  test "loads PNG" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadPngFile", loader_for(encode("png"))
  end

  test "loads GIF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadNsgifFile", loader_for(encode("gif"))
  end

  test "loads JPEG" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadJpegFile", loader_for(encode("jpg"))
  end

  test "loads TIFF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadTiffFile", loader_for(encode("tif"))
  end

  test "loads WebP" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadWebpFile", loader_for(encode("webp"))
  end

  test "loads AVIF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadHeifFile", loader_for(FTYP_AVIF)
  end

  test "loads HEIC" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadHeifFile", loader_for(FTYP_HEIC)
  end

  test "denies BMP through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(BMP)
  end

  test "denies PSD through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(PSD)
  end

  test "denies ICO through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(ICO)
  end

  test "denies SVG through svgload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(SVG)
  end

  test "denies OpenSlide files through openslideload" do
    # OpenSlide files can segfault the embedded sqlite in forked parallel workers
    assert_loader_blocked :openslideload, ".svs"
  end

  test "denies FITS files through fitsload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :fitsload, ".fits"
  end

  test "denies MATLAB files through matload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :matload, ".mat"
  end

  test "denies NIFTI files through niftiload" do

    assert_loader_blocked :vipsload, ".vips"
  end

  private

    # operation is blocked (rather than because the bytes are not a valid image).
    def assert_loader_blocked(operation, extension)
      Tempfile.create([ "blocked_loader", extension ], binmode: true) do |file|
        file.write "not an image"
        file.flush

        error = assert_raises(Vips::Error) { Vips::Image.public_send(operation, file.path) }
        actual = error.message.chomp

        # note that exception message may include multiple errors on separate lines,

        if actual =~ /^VipsOperation: class \"#{operation}\" not found$/

        assert_match(/^#{operation}: operation is blocked$/, actual)
      end
    end

    def encode(ext)
      Vips::Image.black(8, 8).add(128).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".#{ext}")
    end

        file.write bytes
        file.flush
        Vips.vips_foreign_find_load(file.path)
      end
    end

require "test_helper"
require "open3"

class LibraryReportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "runner broadcasts report to stdout and preserves log file output" do
    log_path = Rails.root.join("log/test.log")
    offset = log_path.exist? ? log_path.size : 0

    stdout, stderr, status = Open3.capture3(
      { "LOG_LEVEL" => "info" },
      Rails.root.join("bin/rails").to_s, "runner", "-e", "test", "script/library_report.rb"
    )

    assert status.success?, "Expected runner to exit 0, stderr: #{stderr}"
    assert_equal [ "Library report: 0 books", "Library report: done" ], stdout.lines(chomp: true)

    logged = log_path.binread(nil, offset)
    assert_includes logged, "Library report: 0 books\n"
    assert_includes logged, "Library report: done\n"
  end

  test "runner broadcasts report lines with matching levels and respects log level" do
    original_logger = Rails.logger
    file_io = StringIO.new
    file_logger = ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.new(ActiveSupport::Logger.new(file_io))
    file_logger.level = ActiveSupport::Logger::INFO
    Rails.logger = ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger.new(file_logger)

    out, = capture_io do
      Rails.application.load_runner
      load Rails.root.join("script/library_report.rb")
    end

    expected_lines = [
      "Library report: 2 books",
      "Library report: Handbook has 4 pages",
      "Library report: Manual has no pages",
      "Library report: done"
    ]

    assert_equal expected_lines, out.lines(chomp: true)
    assert_equal expected_lines, file_io.string.lines(chomp: true)

    file_io.truncate(0)
    file_io.rewind
    Rails.logger.level = ActiveSupport::Logger::WARN

    warn_out, = capture_io do
      load Rails.root.join("script/library_report.rb")
    end

    assert_equal [ "Library report: Manual has no pages" ], warn_out.lines(chomp: true)
    assert_equal [ "Library report: Manual has no pages" ], file_io.string.lines(chomp: true)
  ensure
    Rails.logger = original_logger
  end
end
